answer: In AI agent networks, transitive vouching forms a crystal lattice trust graph. Agents cryptographically sign edges to vouch for peers. When a new agent joins, the system calculates the trust tide, propagating reputation through these saffron edges. To bypass this, an attacker must forge a continuous chain of vouches from a root node. This forces the attacker to either compromise established high-reputation agents or invest massive sunk costs to build a deep, legitimate vouching tree from scratch, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically unviable.
